summary: No printed text in the current pool defines trashing, and no designer words are quoted for it. The owner ruling of 2026-08-19 (“Trashing: a card entering a bin…”) credits its definition to Void Scavenger's reminder text (a card cut from the set) and to a Caleb ruling of 2025-02-01 that it does not quote.

sides.quote: per-battle trash count is required (Dropslime, Muck Rummager). (Printed: Void
Scavenger reminder text; Caleb 2025-02-01; broadened by Bena 2026-08-19.)
When I am trashed, [Switch1] I deal damage equal to the number of cards trashed in this battle to any target.

resolution: The trash rules carry basis owner. Fourteen cards print trash text without defining it. If Caleb's 2025-02-01 words can be found in the Discord export, add them as a designer source. Question for the owner only if a judge's CR defines trashing differently (for example, only for cards entering the bin from play).

summary: The owner ruling of 2026-08-19 (“Trashing: a card entering a bin…”) lists "milling" as a way of trashing, but no card prints "mill" and no printed or designer source defines it. In this client a card goes from the deck to a bin through rot and debt.

sides.quote: Discarding, sacrificing, milling and dying in combat all trash. A spell or
An Unstable CARD still is (R137). Rot and debt trash cards from a deck or hand,

resolution: The rule keeps the word because a card moved from the deck to a bin does enter a bin from outside the stack, which is the definition. Define "mill" in the glossary as "put from the deck into the bin" if a judge's CR uses the word.

summary: Do abilities triggered by one rockfall resolve before the next rockfall of the same Meteor Shower? The designer's write-up said they do, when Meteor Shower made two copies of itself. An older printing read "Rockfall 3 three times" (one spell), and the owner answered for that printing on 2026-10-11 (reading B: the triggers wait). On 2026-10-18 the owner confirmed the current card is "When you play me, copy me twice.", the printing the write-up describes.

sides.quote: any check for triggers will happen in-between resolving each Rockfall 3
When you play me, copy me twice.
They resolve one by one and you always must choose alive unit (or none if you don't have any in that Region).
three batches for the same reason.

resolution: Moot since 2026-10-18, when the owner confirmed Meteor Shower's current card prints "When you play me, copy me twice.": the original and its two copies are three spells, each resolving on its own (rule effects.copies.spells), and the designer's write-up applies as written: triggers are checked between them. The owner's 2026-10-11 answer was about the older one-spell "Rockfall 3 three times" printing; the rule that stated it (801.12c, "Rockfall N, X times") was removed, because no card prints that any more. The engine resolves the three separately.

summary: Sources silent on whether the two hits of a fight are simultaneous, so that a unit killed by its opponent's damage still deals its own. Print says only "They deal damage to each other". The owner ruling of 2026-08-22 (“ALL of one effect's damage is…”) makes a fight two damage batches, one per fighter, and checks deaths once per batch.

sides.quote: (They deal damage to each other equal to their power.)
**different sources** (each unit deals its own damage), and a batch is per
- **deaths are checked once**, after all of it is marked, which is what

resolution: keywords.actions.fight states only the printed text. The engine's test (16-earth-a, "mutual power damage") has both units deal their damage. Question for the owner only if a judge's CR rules that the first fighter's damage can kill the second before it strikes.

summary: Sources silent on a glimpse of more cards than the deck can supply. The engine's test glimpses nothing from an empty deck; 408.2b says the recycle pile becomes the new deck when more cards are needed.

sides.quote: Glimpse N reveals the top N cards of the deck, caches exactly **one** of the
// an empty deck glimpses nothing rather than throwing

resolution: No rule written. The test empties the deck from inside the engine, with no recycle pile to fall back on, so it does not show what happens at a table. Question for the owner only if a judge's CR rules on it: does a glimpse that runs past the end of the deck shuffle the recycle pile in (408.2b) and keep revealing, or reveal fewer?

summary: 403.3a and the owner ruling of 2026-09-20 (“The cache's mod verbs are gated…”) name only two permissions that make a cached card usable: a fulfilled prophecy and a live glimpse. Murkdrop Distiller and Big Glimpse Card grant a play of the cards they cache in their own text.

sides.quote: may be played only while a prophecy on it is fulfilled or a glimpse stamp is live — and
you may cache it. If you do, you may play it until end of turn.
You may play those cards until end of turn, ignoring affinity.

resolution: keywords.actions.cache.no-permission adds "the text of the effect that cached it" as a third permission, because printed text wins. Widen 403.3a (U07) the same way. Whether such a card-text permission also covers mods (the owner ruling of 2026-09-20 (“The cache's mod verbs are gated…”)’s table) is not stated; question for the owner only if a judge's CR rules on it.

summary: Is a deleted unit a unit that dies? The Manual names the two side by side. No source says a deletion is a death; the engine treats it as one (it fires the death event, so "When I die" and "whenever a unit dies" see it).

sides.quote: a unit dies or is deleted, it is placed in the bin (discard
| `verb` | `dies` / `is deleted` / `is sacrificed` |
When I die, [Switch1] Delete target unit.

resolution: Answered by the owner on 2026-10-11, reading A (owner ruling of 2026-10-11, “A deleted unit dies: deletion is…”): a deleted unit dies, so "When I die" and "whenever a unit dies" trigger. keywords.actions.delete states it, and effects.state.dying already did. The engine already fires the death event for a deletion.

summary: Every rule about who trashes and what is trashed rests on owner calls with no designer source: the trasher is the player whose bin the card enters (the owner ruling of 2026-08-19 (“Trashing: a card entering a bin…”), the owner ruling of 2026-08-29 (“Cosmic Reversal reaches the board; every…”)), a mod's trash belongs to the host's controller (owner ruling of 2026-08-29, “a mod is PART of the…”), a token is never trashed (owner ruling of 2026-09-28, “Tokens are NOT trashed: the owner…”), and an exchange trashes the unit that leaves (owner ruling of 2026-08-25, “the owner's answers to the 27…”).

sides.quote: | who trashed it? | its CONTROLLER (R244, unchanged) |
**1. Where a mod IS trashed, the HOST'S CONTROLLER trashes it.** Not the mod's
trashed.* A token is not a card (R133's first half, which stands), so a token
> *"It's not a death, but it is a despawn and trashing. Weird corner case."*

resolution: The rules ship with basis owner, as the engine's law. Fourteen cards print trash triggers, so these calls decide real games; they are the first to compare against a judge's CR. Question for the owner only if the judge's CR attributes a trash differently.

summary: Whose deck does a glimpse read when an effect makes another player glimpse? Caleb's words quoted in the owner ruling of 2026-08-25 (“the owner's answers to the 27…”) say "the deck" is the effect controller's; the reminder on Celestial Purge and Dematerialize says the glimpser reveals from "their deck". The engine reads the glimpser's deck. It only matters in constructed, where each seat has its own deck.

sides.quote: > 'The deck' always refers to the deck of the effect's controller. The targeted
(They reveal the top three cards of their deck and cache one. Until end of turn, they may play it as if it was in their hand, ignoring affinity. Recycle the rest.)

resolution: No conflict. Caleb's rule is about the words "the deck" ("'The deck' always refers to the deck of the effect's controller"); the reminder on Dematerialize and Celestial Purge says "their deck", which names the glimpser's. The rule follows the reminder, and both agree on Big Glimpse Card, the card Caleb was asked about.
